author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN004634693 (PTHR23358)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Fly 'Tet' gene (FBgn0263392/M9NEY8)

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
erroneous propagation

Unlike mammalian TET, the fly ortholog catalyses demethylation of methyl**adenosine** in DNA.
I.e fly Tet has EC:1.14.11.51 = GO:0141131 DNA N6-methyladenine demethylase activity, and not EC:1.14.11.80 = 5-methylcytosine dioxygenase activity (GO:0070579).  See PMID: 25936838

So either the current 5-methylcytosine dioxygenase activity annotation on PTN004634693 needs moving up the hierarchy a bit to be globally true, or else different branches need annotating with the different activities.

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks!

>Is that because there is no methyC in the genome?

From PMID: 25936838:

Recent studies have suggested that methylation/demethylation at the C-5 position of [cytosine](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/cytosine) in mammals is a dynamic and reversible process controlled by several mechanisms...

Given the important roles of 6mA modification in bacteria, we explore whether 6mA plays a role in eukaryotes. However, previous studies have suggested that the 6mA base is present at extremely low levels in genomic DNA of higher eukaryotes ([Ratel et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867415004353?via%3Dihub#bib20))....

In Drosophila, 5mC modification exists at an extremely low level ([Lyko and Maleszka, 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867415004353?via%3Dihub#bib14)), and the Drosophila Dnmt2-dependent [methylome](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/biochemistry-genetics-and-molecular-biology/methylome) lacks defined DNA 5mC patterns ([Raddatz et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867415004353?via%3Dihub#bib19)). Thus, whether the Drosophila genome has a functional DNA modification remains elusive. In this study, we show that DNA modification 6mA is present in the Drosophila genome at a considerable level...
